name: Plain Language
title: Plain Language
answer: Plain language means rewriting school policies, notices, and forms so families can understand and act on them. It matters because confusing or intimidating wording can leave families unsure, while clear and supportive wording gets better results. AI can help produce plain versions, but a person must check accuracy and preserve any legally required wording.

sections.body: School documents are often written in language that suits lawyers more than parents. Policies, notices, and forms filled with jargon can confuse or intimidate families. The idea is to use an approved AI tool to turn complex text into plain language that most families can read. A staff member then checks the plain version for accuracy and for anything important that may have been lost. This solves the problem of families not acting because they do not understand what the school is telling them.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: A district can use an approved tool to rewrite a policy explanation, a permission form, or a notice at a reading level most families can manage. A staff member reviews the result to confirm it is accurate and complete. Where a legal notice must keep certain wording, the school can add a plain explanation alongside it. The text gives no grade bands for this practice, so it applies to school documents across grade levels. The text also advises checking readability before translating, because a clear English original produces a clearer translation in any language.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text cites a truancy trial showing that plain, supportive language gets better results than legal wording (Lasky-Fink et al., 2021). It also cites research on machine translated school notices, which found that translations of complex English text often backfired with Spanish speaking families (Rodriguez-Castro, 2018). The author of that research proposed checking readability before translating. The text does not give an evidence label for this idea. These findings support the practice of plain language before translation.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: AI can draft a plain version, but a staff member must check that it is accurate and that nothing important was lost. Legal notices may need to keep certain wording, so the plain explanation is added alongside rather than replacing it. The district should use an approved tool rather than any available tool. The decision to approve and send a rewritten document stays with a person. The text does not offer legal advice, and it describes practice rather than a guarantee of outcomes.
